source.author: verg
source.text: Ipse, sedens niveo candentis limine Phoebi, dona recognoscit populorum aptatque superbis postibus; incedunt victae longo ordine gentes, quam variae linguis, habitu tam vestis et armis.
source.text_original: Ipse, sedens niveo candentis limine Phoebi, / dona recognoscit populorum aptatque superbis / postibus; incedunt victae longo ordine gentes, / quam variae linguis, habitu tam vestis et armis.
source.text_english: He himself, seated on the gleaming threshold of snow-white Phoebus, reviews the gifts of the peoples and arranges them on the proud doors; conquered nations advance in long procession, as varied in their tongues as in their dress and armor.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: ubi tunc totius orbis homines ab India usque ad Britanniam, a rigida septentrionis plaga usque ad feruores Atlantici oceani, tam innumerabiles populi et tantarum gentium multitudines quam uariae linguis, habitu tam uestis et armis?
reuse.text_original: ubi tunc totius orbis homines ab India usque ad Britanniam, a rigida septentrionis plaga usque ad feruores Atlantici oceani, tam innumerabiles populi et tantarum gentium multitudines quam uariae linguis, habitu tam uestis et armis?
reuse.text_english: where then were the men of the whole world, from India to Britain, from the frigid region of the north to the heats of the Atlantic Ocean, those countless peoples and throngs of so many nations, differing as much in languages as in dress and arms?
